docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Admission to this bar does not excuse local counsel. Local counsel is required whenever the lawyer appearing does not reside or keep a principal office in the district, whether or not that lawyer is admitted here. docs.x: E.D. Wash.. Hearing dates: 30 days for ordinary motions, 50 for dispositive ones. docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Confer by phone or in person, and certify it. Emails and letters don’t satisfy the meet-and-confer rule. A certificate of conference at the end of the motion gives the date, manner, participants, why no agreement was reached, and that talks ended in an impasse. Skipping the conference without bad faith by the other side breaks Local Rule AT-3. (CV-7(h), (i))

docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Discovery doesn’t pause for pending motions. Within 7 days, publicly file a redacted version unless the whole document is confidential. (Local Rule CV-5(a)(7))

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Dispositive and summary judgment motions have extra content

The court won’t scour the record for an undesignated dispute, and facts you support are assumed admitted unless controverted. (Local Rule CV-7(a)(1), CV-56)

docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. Biennial registration, $50. Submit the biennial registration when the clerk’s notice arrives, with a $50 fee. docs.t: S.D.W. Va. — You need a sponsor who lives and practices in West Virginia
docs.x: S.D.W. Va.. You need a sponsor who lives and practices in West Virginia. A visiting attorney must associate with a Sponsoring Attorney who is a member of this court’s bar, has a West Virginia law office, and practices primarily in West Virginia. The sponsor signs every paper that requires an attorney’s signature. No motion is required, but the Statement of Visiting Attorney and the fee are due at or before your first appearance, including when you sign a pleading. (LR Civ P 83.6(a))

docs.x: S.D.W. Va.. West Virginia charges its own pro hac vice fee. The West Virginia State Bar’s fee is separate from the court’s and is paid to the State Bar, not the clerk. Under Rule 8 of the state’s admission rules it is currently $350 per applicant per case, plus an annual fee if the admission lasts a year or more. Check the current amounts before you file. docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Finish the court’s online tutorial before seeking pro hac vice
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Finish the court’s online tutorial before seeking pro hac vice. Visiting lawyers must complete N.D. Fla.’s online Attorney Admission Tutorial and review the CM/ECF Attorney User’s Guide before applying. The tutorial can’t be waived, and no substitute training counts. Local counsel isn’t required, and visiting lawyers file their own motion once the registration is processed. The fee is $219 per case. (LR 11.1(E); Attorney Admission Memo)

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Only Florida Bar members can join this court’s bar
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Only Florida Bar members can join this court’s bar. Admission to the N.D. Fla. bar requires good standing in The Florida Bar; a license elsewhere doesn’t qualify, no matter how long you have practiced federally. Everyone else appears pro hac vice in each case. Don’t file or appear before admission or pro hac vice leave, except in an emergency while the application is pending. (LR 11.1(A), (C)–(D))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Use 14-point type
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Use 14-point type. Every document must be double spaced, in at least 14-point font, with one-inch margins and numbered pages. Most districts accept 12-point; this one doesn’t. (LR 5.1(C))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Hold a real conference before filing, and certify it
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Hold a real conference before filing, and certify it. Before filing, confer meaningfully with opposing counsel. An email sent at or near filing doesn’t count, and a written conference ordinarily allows at least 24 hours to respond. The motion or memorandum must include a certificate, under a separate heading, confirming compliance and the results. (LR 7.1(B)–(C))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — 8,000 words, with a word-count certificate
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. 8,000 words, with a word-count certificate. Memoranda are capped at 8,000 words, including headings, footnotes, and quotations, and must include a certificate of the word count. A motion over 500 words counts against the memorandum’s limit. (LR 7.1(F))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — No replies without leave, except on summary judgment
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. No replies without leave, except on summary judgment. A party ordinarily may not file a reply. Leave is granted only in extraordinary circumstances and must be obtained before tendering the reply. Replies are limited to 3,200 words. (LR 7.1(I))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — No separate statement of facts on summary judgment
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. No separate statement of facts on summary judgment. Facts go in the memorandum, written as in an appellate brief, with pinpoint record citations. Neither side may file a separate statement of facts or a separate response to one. The opposition is due in 21 days, with no extra 3 days. (LR 56.1(B)–(C))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Fee motions are two-step, and the clock starts at judgment
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Fee motions are two-step, and the clock starts at judgment. Move for entitlement within 14 days after judgment; an appeal doesn’t extend the deadline. Fees are awarded only on contemporaneous, detailed time records to the nearest tenth hour, and the amount phase requires an independent attorney’s declaration. (LR 54.1)

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Never write to the judge, including by email
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Never write to the judge, including by email. A request for action can never be made by letter, and “letter” includes email. Sentencing letters go to the probation office. (LR 7.1(A), (M))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Tell the court the moment a case settles
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Tell the court the moment a case settles. Notify the court immediately of a settlement, a motion resolved by agreement, or an expected motion to continue, and by phone if a trial or hearing is near. If notice comes less than 2 days before a jury panel reports, juror fees and mileage can be assessed against the party, the lawyer, or both. (LR 16.2)

docs.t: D. Guam — Pro hac vice renewal fee, due January 1
docs.x: D. Guam. Pro hac vice renewal fee, due January 1. A lawyer admitted, or previously admitted, under subsection (d) owes an annual renewal fee the court sets, due on or before January 1. docs.x: D.N.H.. Objections are due 14 days from filing, or they’re waived. Objections are due 14 days after the motion is filed, or 30 days for summary judgment. The clock runs from filing, not service, and the court deems late objections waived. (LR 7.1(b))

docs.x: D.N.H.. Replies: as of right only for dispositive motions. On dispositive motions, a reply of up to 10 pages is due within 7 days of the objection. On nondispositive motions, move for leave within 7 days and attach a proposed reply of up to 5 pages. (LR 7.1(e))

docs.t: D.N.H. — One motion per filing
docs.x: D.N.H.. One motion per filing. Each motion must say “motion” in its title. Don’t combine motions seeking distinct relief, and never fold an affirmative motion into an objection. (LR 7.1(a)(1))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Seek concurrence and say “assented-to”

docs.t: D.N.H. — Pro hac vice: one motion per lawyer, with years of admission
docs.x: D.N.H.. Pro hac vice: one motion per lawyer, with years of admission. Local counsel files a separate motion for each visiting lawyer, with an affidavit listing every court of admission and the year, and disclosing prior pro hac vice denials or revocations. The $100 fee per lawyer isn’t refunded. Local counsel signs all filings and attends all proceedings. (LR 83.2(b))

docs.x: D.N.H.. Two disclosure statements, filed separately. docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Renewal fee every two years, due February 15
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Renewal fee every two years, due February 15. Unless you were admitted pro hac vice, pay the fee the court sets every two years, due on or before February 15. After a missed payment the court sends a 30-day notice that adds a late fee, then a second 30-day notice. If you still don’t pay, you are removed from the roll and must qualify for admission anew. The fee is $30 per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. (D.N. Mar. I. LR 83.5(c))

docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Oppose within 14 days, or concede. Oppositions are due 14 days after service. The court may disregard and strike a late opposition and may treat the failure to oppose on time as an admission that the motion is meritorious. (LR 7.1(c)(2))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — A motion is heard on a Thursday, at least 34 days out
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. A motion is heard on a Thursday, at least 34 days out. Motion day is Thursday. A motion is noticed for hearing on the first Thursday at least 34 days after it is filed, unless you arrange another date with the docket clerk. Non-hearing motions, such as motions to extend time and stipulated motions, are decided on the papers. (LR 7.1(b)(1), (c)(1))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Put the hearing date and time on the first page
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Put the hearing date and time on the first page. The first page of every motion, opposition, reply, or other filing aimed at a hearing must show the hearing date and time, for example “Hearing: June 29, 2017 / Time: 9:00 a.m.” (LR 5.2(e))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — The reply is 7 days, and then nothing more
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. The reply is 7 days, and then nothing more. The reply is due 7 days after the opposition is served and is limited to 10 pages. No further filings are accepted without leave, and any filed in violation of the rule are stricken. (LR 7.1(c)(3), (4))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Briefs are 25 pages, replies 10
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Briefs are 25 pages, replies 10. A brief or memorandum may not exceed 25 pages, and a reply 10. Anything over 10 pages needs a table of contents and a table of authorities. To go over, move first, without attaching the brief. Excess pages are stricken. (LR 7.1(d))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — An extension motion has a required caption
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. An extension motion has a required caption. The caption must read, in capitals and bold, MOTION TO EXTEND (OR SHORTEN) TIME UNDER LOCAL RULE 7.1(f). State the earlier extensions, the reasons, and the effect on other deadlines. Without a stipulation, certify that you tried to meet and confer. An emergency motion (action within 48 hours) also needs phone and email notice. (LR 7.1(f))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Proposed orders go by email, not CM/ECF

Miss the first deadline and the document is inadmissible. Miss the second and you waive your objection. (LR 16.5(a)(4))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Filing deadline: midnight, Northern Mariana Islands time
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Filing deadline: midnight, Northern Mariana Islands time. Electronic filing must be completed before midnight local time in the Northern Mariana Islands for a filing to be timely that day. The Northern Mariana Islands are on Chamorro Standard Time (UTC+10) and don’t observe daylight saving time, so they are 15 hours ahead of Eastern Standard Time and 14 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time. (Local Rules, Appendix A § 3)

docs.t: D. Utah — Register and pay by July 1 every year
docs.x: D. Utah. Register and pay by July 1 every year. To keep active status, register through CM/ECF and pay the annual fee, set by the court, by July 1 each year. Active status also means accepting pro bono assignments unless a government employer prohibits it. You owe nothing until 12 months after admission, and federal attorneys are exempt from the fee. The fee is $30 per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. (DUCivR 83-1.2)

docs.t: D. Utah — Motion and memorandum in one document
docs.x: D. Utah. Motion and memorandum in one document. The motion and its supporting memorandum are a single document, opening with a separate section stating the relief sought and the grounds. Only a few motions, such as an unopposed extension filed before the deadline, skip the facts and authority. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(1))

docs.t: D. Utah — No motions inside responses, and no joinders
docs.x: D. Utah. No motions inside responses, and no joinders. Every motion, including a Rule 56(d) request or a cross-motion, is filed separately. A “Notice of Joinder” is improper: file your own motion and incorporate the other side’s arguments by reference. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(3), (a)(8))

docs.t: D. Utah — Limits and deadlines depend on the motion

docs.t: D. Utah — Stipulated extensions are ineffective without an order
docs.x: D. Utah. Stipulated extensions are ineffective without an order. To extend a briefing deadline, file a stipulated motion before the time runs out and get an order. No stipulation that affects the course of the case takes effect until the court approves it. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(5), 83-4)

docs.t: D. Utah — Discovery disputes: short-form motion within 45 days
docs.x: D. Utah. Discovery disputes: short-form motion within 45 days. Send a prompt written deficiency letter that asks to meet and confer. If the dispute persists, file a Short Form Discovery Motion of 500 words or less within 45 days of that letter, or it can be automatically denied. The response is due 5 business days later. (DUCivR 37-1)

docs.t: D. Utah — Don’t move to strike evidence
docs.x: D. Utah. Don’t move to strike evidence. A motion to strike evidence in another party’s brief is improper. Raise an evidentiary objection in your response or reply, or within 7 days after new evidence appears in a reply. (DUCivR 7-1(b))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Put “motion” in the title, or it won’t be considered
docs.x: D. Vt.. Put “motion” in the title, or it won’t be considered. The court will not consider any motion that lacks the word “motion” in its title. (L.R. 7(a)(1))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Oppositions: 30 days for dispositive, 14 for others
docs.x: D. Vt.. Oppositions: 30 days for dispositive, 14 for others. Oppositions to dispositive motions are due 30 days after service; all others, 14 days. Replies of up to 10 pages are due 14 days after the opposition. (L.R. 7(a)(3))

docs.x: D. Vt.. First and Second Circuit lawyers can join the bar outright. Members of any First or Second Circuit district court bar may apply for full admission, with a sponsor’s affidavit, a certificate of good standing, and the fee. (L.R. 83.1(a)(1)(B))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Pro hac vice: local counsel signs and attends everything
docs.x: D. Vt.. Pro hac vice: local counsel signs and attends everything. Local counsel files the motion with your affidavit listing every bar you’ve joined, a certificate of good standing, and a non-refundable fee. Local counsel signs all filings and attends all proceedings unless waived, and is your agent for service. (L.R. 83.1(b))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Discovery schedule: 45 or 75 days, or discovery is waived
docs.x: D. Vt.. Discovery schedule: 45 or 75 days, or discovery is waived. File the joint Discovery Schedule within the earlier of 75 days after any defendant is served or 45 days after any defendant appears. Failure to strictly comply waives the need for discovery, and the case is set for trial. Discovery runs no more than 8 months after the last answer, and a motion to dismiss doesn’t stay it. (L.R. 26(a)(2), (5))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Summary judgment needs a numbered fact statement
docs.x: D. Vt.. Summary judgment needs a numbered fact statement. File a separate, concise statement in numbered paragraphs, each with a citation to admissible evidence. docs.t: D.V.I. — Annual renewal fee, $45
docs.x: D.V.I.. Annual renewal fee, $45. An annual renewal fee of $45 is required, per the FJC’s 2024 compilation of the court’s fee schedule. We haven’t read this rule ourselves, so confirm with the clerk. (D.V.I. LR 83.1(c)(2); FJC 2024)

docs.t: D.V.I. — Three pro hac vice cases a year, maximum
docs.x: D.V.I.. Three pro hac vice cases a year, maximum. A lawyer may be admitted pro hac vice in no more than three cases per calendar year, and not at all while already in three active cases. Every filing needs local counsel’s signature and is deemed approved by local counsel. (LRCi 83.1(b)(2))

docs.t: D.V.I. — No separate memorandum; argument goes in the motion
docs.x: D.V.I.. No separate memorandum; argument goes in the motion. A motion includes the relief, background, and argument with authority. Separate memoranda aren’t allowed, and further briefing needs leave before filing. (LRCi 7.1(a)(1))

docs.t: D.V.I. — Every motion needs a draft order, with real dates
docs.x: D.V.I.. Every motion needs a draft order, with real dates. Attach a draft order stating the specific relief. For extensions, state the actual new deadline date. (LRCi 7.1(a)(5))

docs.t: D.V.I. — Rule 12 and 56 responses run from filing
docs.x: D.V.I.. Rule 12 and 56 responses run from filing. Responses are due 21 days after the motion is filed for Rule 12 and Rule 56 motions; 14 days after service for most others; 7 days after filing for motions in limine. (LRCi 6.1(b))

docs.t: D.V.I. — 20 pages or 6,000 words; ask two days ahead
docs.x: D.V.I.. 20 pages or 6,000 words; ask two days ahead. Leave to exceed the limit must be sought at least two days before filing. Over 20 pages requires a word-count certificate. (LRCi 7.1(b))

docs.t: D.V.I. — One of each
docs.x: D.V.I.. One of each. Without leave, a party may file only one Rule 12(b)(2)–(6) motion, one Rule 56 motion, and one motion in limine. (LRCi 7.1(c))

docs.t: D.V.I. — Seek consent 24 hours before filing
docs.x: D.V.I.. Seek consent 24 hours before filing. Non-dispositive motions must state that consent was sought from each party at least 24 hours before filing, and whether it was given or denied. (LRCi 7.1(e))

docs.t: D.V.I. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: D.V.I.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: D.V.I. — overview
docs.x: D.V.I.. Continuances need alternative dates,LRCi 7.1(f),Consult the other parties and propose several agreeable dates. Oral argument requests go at the end,LRCi 7.1(d),State the request separately at the conclusion of the motion, response, or reply. Post-trial motions need record cites,LRCi 7.1(g),Cite the specific record portions and order transcripts promptly. Holidays include court closures,LRCi 6.1(a),Any day both divisions are closed counts as a legal holiday. Special admission for public-interest work,LRCi 83.1(c),Lawyers representing the V.I. government, public interest groups, or pro bono clients may seek special admission for up to three years. Keep to the schedule,LRCi 83.1(d),Strictly observe all dates. Noncompliance can cost pro hac vice permission.

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Confer first, and say exactly how
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Confer first, and say exactly how. Non-dispositive motions must state the specific efforts made to confer and the other side’s position. A motion may be summarily denied without that. The duty doesn’t apply when a pro se party is involved. (L.R. 7.1(b)(1)(A))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Discovery disputes start with a phone call
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Discovery disputes start with a phone call. After conferring, counsel jointly contact the assigned magistrate judge for an informal telephonic discovery call. The court allows a written discovery motion only if the call doesn’t resolve it. (L.R. 37.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — 14 days to respond, or risk a confession
docs.x: D. Wyo.. 14 days to respond, or risk a confession. Responses to dispositive and non-dispositive motions are due 14 days after the motion is filed. The court may treat a late or missing response as a confession of the motion. (L.R. 7.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Short limits: 10, 25, 5, and 10
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Short limits: 10, 25, 5, and 10. Briefs on non-dispositive motions run 10 pages and on dispositive motions 25. Replies are due 7 days after the response and capped at 5 pages (non-dispositive) or 10 (dispositive). Reply extensions need extraordinary circumstances. (L.R. 7.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — No replies on motions set for hearing
docs.x: D. Wyo.. No replies on motions set for hearing. If a motion is set for hearing, no reply may be filed. Missing a noticed hearing can be treated as waiving your motion or confessing the one against you. (L.R. 7.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Nothing under seal without prior permission
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Nothing under seal without prior permission. In civil cases, no case or document may be filed under seal or as non-public without prior court authorization or order. (L.R. 5.1(g))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — No stipulated continuances
docs.x: D. Wyo.. No stipulated continuances. Cases aren’t continued on the parties’ stipulation alone. The court must approve, and only on good cause. Any extension request must disclose prior extensions, objections, and a date certain (L.R. 6.1(e)). (L.R. 40.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Local counsel must be in both bars
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Local counsel must be in both bars. Local counsel must belong to the Wyoming State Bar and this court’s bar, appear before anything is filed, move for your admission, and attend every proceeding unless excused. (L.R. 84.2(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. docs.t: D. Mont. — Re-registration fees, and your state license must stay active
docs.x: D. Mont.. Re-registration fees, and your state license must stay active. You must pay the admission fee and any re-registration fees the court imposes, and failing to pay can deactivate your filing privileges. Going inactive, or being suspended, with the State Bar of Montana automatically makes you ineligible here until you are back in good standing. (D. Mont. L.R. 83.1)

docs.t: D. Mont. — Montana counts words, not pages
docs.x: D. Mont.. Montana counts words, not pages. Opening and response briefs: 6,500 words. Replies: 3,250. Any brief of 4,000 words or more needs a table of contents, table of authorities, and exhibit index. Every brief needs a word-count certificate. (L.R. 7.1(d)(2))

docs.t: D. Mont. — Clocks run from docket entry
docs.x: D. Mont.. Clocks run from docket entry. Responses to motions to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, or for summary judgment are due 21 days after docket entry; all others, 14. Replies are due 14 days after the response is docketed. Silence on a non-dispositive motion may be deemed an admission. (L.R. 7.1(d)(1))
